{'translation': 'Bookstore Leave a Book (留下書舍), which was caught up in a national security case, had been suspended for over a month. Today (the 25th), it announced that it would close down as originally scheduled after August 30. The bookstore will resume final operations for five consecutive days from tomorrow (the 26th) to Sunday (the 30th), from 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. daily, with clearance sales.'}

{'translation': 'Leave a Book issued a farewell statement on social media, saying: "Four years pass like a snap of the fingers, yet flowers fall and we still know each other. In books, one finds no golden house, nor a beauty fair as jade. Why force oneself to fulfil lifelong ambitions? Boiling wine and chatting merrily is enough. Facing this final note, tears fall unbidden, words fail me; I can only offer a word of thanks. Take care."'}

{'translation': 'Opened four years ago, Leave a Book announced last month that it would close at the end of August. One day later, national security police visited and alleged that the bookstore had violated the offence of sedition under Article 23 of the Basic Law, arresting three people from the bookstore on suspicion of committing sedition under Article 23. Two people from Garden Bookstore (田園書屋) were also arrested in the same case. Garden Bookstore, with a 50-year history, also announced at the end of last month that it would close upon the expiry of its lease. The publication involved is reportedly "The Red Flower\'s Bloom: Identity and Belonging in the Xi Jinping Era" written by Chinese-American journalist Eileen Feng.\n\nNote: 田園書屋 retains its literal translation "Garden Bookstore" or the original English name "Tian Yuan Bookstore" based on availability. Placeholder for final translation if conventional Hong Kong name is found.'}

{'translation': 'Leave a Book was founded in 2022 by veteran journalist Sham Wan-wah (岑蘊華) and several former Stand News reporters. At that time, media outlets including Apple Daily, Stand News and Citizen News had already ceased operations one after another. The bookstore was named "Leave" (留下) and "Book House" (書舍), symbolising "leaving words behind" (留下書寫). The bookstore primarily stocked books related to journalism and the media, and also regularly held talks and author sharing sessions.'}

{'translation': 'On the 14th of last month, Leave a Book announced that it would close on August 30, citing the difficulty of gauging the red lines as one of the reasons for shutting down.'}
